reviews.one_line_contribution: A quantified measurement, in net success points against a token-matched verbatim-injection comparator, of how much of an execution-trained experience rewriter's benefit survives a change of reader along three separately manipulated axes (scaffold, capability at fixed backbone, backbone), plus a non-inferiority test of importing that rewriter against the held-out backbone collecting its own experience for the same GPU-hours.
reviews.closest_prior_work: 2605.30723, 'Skill is Not One-Size-Fits-All: Model-Aware Skill Alignment for LLM Agents' (verified via `s2cli.py paper`, 2026-05-29, cit 2, s2+hf). Its thesis is the proposal's headline: skills must be adapted per backbone, and it does that with exactly the mechanism under study, a lightweight trained rewriter per backbone. The proposal's novelty argument rests on an unverifiable negative about this paper ('never applies a rewriter trained against one backbone to another, never reports how much of the gain is retained'); I could verify the paper exists and what its abstract claims, but not the absence of a swapped-rewriter ablation, because section text needs WebSearch, which is unavailable in this session, and WebFetch is blocked. If that ablation is in the paper, this proposal is a reject. Two further verified papers eat into the remaining margin: 2605.23899 (verified, cit 15) already reports a systematic extractor x target-agent matrix with non-uniform extractors and targets and non-trivial negative transfer, i.e. the writer x reader matrix for static skills; and 2605.30785 AdaCoM (verified, cit 5) already reports a capability-indexed reader specificity for a trained context manager ('agents with higher vanilla ReAct performance benefit from higher-fidelity context preservation, whereas lower-performing agents require more aggressive compression'), which is the P2b axis in another guise. 2606.01139 SkillRevise (verified, cit 12) is correctly named as the opposite prediction, but note it transfers revised skills across executors, not the reviser, so it is a weaker threat than the proposal treats it as. What is left genuinely unmeasured is the retained-gain fraction of a trained rewriter on a held-out reader with proximity and capability separated, and the matched-GPU-hour self-collection break-even. That is measurement novelty on an expected direction, not a new claim: the home literature already establishes that data filtered by rejection sampling against one policy is that policy's (2404.14367, 'Preference Fine-Tuning of LLMs Should Leverage Suboptimal, On-Policy Data', and the on-policy-distillation line generally, found via the literature command), so P1 confirming is close to the default expectation.
reviews.strongest_objection: The axis separation the whole design exists to deliver is verified at a precision coarser than the tolerance it asserts, and the two predictions that carry it cannot resolve. (a) Headroom matching: A' and B are admitted as 'verified within +/-5 net of A at k=0' and A''s thinking budget is tuned so k=0 sits in an 8-12 net window, but C0 is run at 2 seeds (the proposal's own noise table: +/-8) and the A'' tuning cell at 4 seeds (+/-5.7). A +/-5 tolerance checked with a +/-8 instrument, and a 4-net-wide window set with a +/-5.7 instrument, are not verification; the P2a defense that 'headroom is matched by construction' is therefore unsupported, and any I(R_A,A) - I(R_A,B) gap can be read as a headroom difference the guard failed to exclude. (b) Power: as the proposal's own noise convention states, cross-reader differences of increments carry +/-5.7 at 8 seeds while the P2a/P2b margins are 6, so under the stated decision rule ('falsified' = CI upper bound below the margin) falsification requires a point estimate below ~0.3 net. Full retention falsifies only about half the time and the substantively interesting middle - the rewriter keeping 60-70% on the foreign backbone - is permanently indeterminate. The stated remedy ('if a headline cell's measured half-width exceeds its margin, extend to 12 seeds') does not trigger here, because 5.7 < 6. (c) P4 is close to entailed: Delta = [S(B,C_selfcost) - S(B,C_vtok)] - I(R_A,B), and the proposal's own Measurement-C numbers put the first bracket near +8, so the non-inferiority test fails only if I(R_A,B) >= ~13 net, i.e. the imported rewriter helps the held-out backbone more than Gate 0 demands of its own training reader. No stated mechanism can produce that, so P4 will confirm almost regardless of the truth, which is precisely what the round's binding rule forbids. Secondary but real: Gate 0 with C_vtok = k=1 asks a ~300-token plan to beat the k=7 verbatim level (+19.5 over static3) at a fifth of the tokens; the proposal concedes this, and the fallback path (prompted R_0 becomes the transferred subject) silently changes the object of study from a trained rewriter to a prompt.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Three concrete changes, none of which needs a new idea. (1) Run every k=0 matching cell (A, A', A'', B) at 8 seeds and pre-register the admission tolerance at or above the realized half-width, so 'verified within +/-5' means something; better, report all cross-reader increments headroom-normalised (increment divided by 1 - S(r,C_vtok)) as the primary reading and the raw net points as secondary, so the axis separation does not depend on the matching succeeding. (2) Set the P2a/P2b margins at twice the realized half-width of the cross-reader difference (or run those six increment cells at 16 seeds) and pre-register the falsifier as an upper bound below ~3 net, so 'the rewriter keeps most of its increment on the foreign backbone' is a resolvable outcome rather than an indeterminate one. (3) Replace P4's fixed -5 margin with one derived from the measured S(B,C_selfcost) - S(B,C_vtok) gap, or compare C_selfcost against C_RA at matched consumer tokens, so the verbatim bracket cannot absorb the comparison; and drop P4's claim to independence entirely unless I(R_A,B) clears the threshold that makes it so. Beyond that, verifying the body of 2605.30723 (and stating what it does and does not swap) before submission is not optional: the entire novelty case is one unread paper away from collapsing.
reviews.missing_baseline: A reader's own rewriter on the proximity and capability readers: R_{A'} trained in the loop with A' and R_{A''} trained in the loop with A''. As designed, A' and A'' only ever receive the imported R_A, so there is no own-rewriter reference on those readers, and I(R_A,A'') can fall for two indistinguishable reasons - the rewriter is A-specific, or A'' is simply less improvable by any rewriter (the k=0 guard equates baseline success, not the size of the increment any rewriter can buy). Without that reference cell, P2b ('capability loses less than backbone') is not a clean comparison: on the backbone axis the design has the own-rewriter anchor (R_B on B) that it lacks on the capability axis. A reviewer would also ask for a reader-side adaptation arm at matched cost - target-side reader alignment (2608.17050) or MemHarness-style reconstruction (2607.28272, named as an allowed reimplementation in the brief) - since the practical alternative to importing a foreign writer-side rewriter is adapting on the reader side, and for the obvious constructive control, a rewriter trained against both readers' execution feedback, which is what a negative P1 result would immediately motivate.
reviews.preprint_collision: No verified collision, but the proposal's check leans on negatives it did not establish. Queries I ran, all answered by the literature command (s2cli.py, s2=ok hf=ok); WebSearch was unavailable in this session, so no query was answered by channel (b), and no section text was read. (1) recent, mechanism: 'rewriter trained against one reader transfers to held-out reader backbone execution feedback' -> 2608.17050 (cross-model memory reuse needs a target-side reader adapter), 2605.30723, 2602.11220 (RL rewriting agent aligning rewritten data to one model's own generation distribution - a model-specific rewriter in the SFT-data setting, not in the proposal's related work), 2606.05633; nothing reporting a held-out-reader retention fraction. (2) closest named method: 'model-aware skill alignment lightweight rewriter per backbone' -> 2605.30723 (the closest card), 2606.01139, 2608.06880 SkillAligner (execution-time adaptation of retrieved skills, missing from the proposal's related work), 2605.23657 OpenSkillEval ('performance benefits depend heavily on model and framework combinations' - the backbone x scaffold interaction the proposal proposes to discover), 2605.09359, 2604.04804. (3) recent, matched cost: 'how much of the gain does a held-out model retain imported adapter versus self-collected data at matched compute' -> nothing relevant (2609.01437, 2609.00787, 2607.25271); reported as empty, which is not evidence of novelty. (4) home vocabulary: 'rejection sampling fine-tuning data is policy specific on-policy distillation outperforms off-policy data from another model' -> 2404.14367, 2602.15260, 2511.04285, 2505.24850; these establish the direction of P1 as the field's default expectation without measuring it for a rewriter. (5) recent, mechanism/axes: 'context rewriter trained for one agent evaluated on a different agent scaffold change versus backbone change retained benefit' -> 2608.26218 'Same Model, Different Harness' (harness change alters success at fixed weights - directly relevant to the A/A' scaffold axis and uncited), 2607.03691, 2605.30723. Verified by ID with s2cli.py paper: 2605.30723, 2606.01139 (cit 12), 2604.07487, 2605.30785 (cit 5), 2609.01437, 2607.28272, 2505.09930, 2208.10160, 2605.23899 (cit 15) - all nine exist and match the proposal's descriptions of their abstracts. Confirmed as existing through search hits but not individually verified: 2605.09359, 2604.04804, 2608.06880, 2605.23657, 2608.26218, 2602.11220. Not verified at all: 2605.27922 (Harness-Bench), 2604.15877, 2605.24117. Judgment on the proposal's own check: it is above average for this round - it names IDs, labels query classes including the required home-vocabulary search, and verified AdaCoM by ID - but its load-bearing statements are negatives about paper bodies it never read ('2605.30723 never applies a rewriter trained against one backbone to another'; '2606.01139 never quantifies what is retained'), and it missed 2605.23657, 2608.06880, 2608.26218 and 2602.11220. An unverified negative about the single closest paper is the weakest possible foundation for a novelty claim, and I could not repair it from this node.
